questions.0.explain.t: The master key never leaves the KMS, and the encrypted data key can travel with the data.

questions.0.options.0.t: Encrypting the data with a data key, and encrypting that key with a KMS master key

questions.0.options.1.t: Encrypting the same data twice with the same key, to double the protection

questions.0.options.2.t: Keeping the data key next to the data, in plain text, in the same bucket

questions.1.explain.t: Encrypting is pointless if the key's policy is too permissive.

questions.1.options.0.t: Whoever can use the key can decrypt everything it protects

questions.1.options.1.t: Because KMS keys expire after a few hours by default

questions.1.options.2.t: Because KMS is slow and any extra access delays the application

questions.1.options.3.t: Because each key takes up space and storage is limited

questions.1.q.t: Why is access to the key in the KMS so critical?

questions.2.explain.t: Separation of duties and rotation reduce the impact of any abuse.

questions.2.options.0.t: Automatic rotation and separation between who administers and who uses the key

questions.2.options.1.t: Sharing the key by email with whoever needs to use it

questions.2.options.2.t: Never rotating, so as not to invalidate data that is already encrypted

questions.2.options.3.t: Using the same key in all environments to simplify operations
